resources.string: Style
Keyboard themes
Light, dark and AMOLED themes, colors, background images, import and export
Keyboard font
Google Fonts, or import your own font file
Icons
Change any tool icon or key icon, or install an icon pack
Keys
Key corner radius
How round the corners of the keys are
0 gives square keys. 28 gives keys with a full pill shape.
Key label font size
Scale of the labels on the keys
This changes the size of every label on the keys. The popup bubbles have their own font size under Key press → Key popup.
Key hint font size
Scale of the small hint character in the corner of each key
Letter case on keys
Draw the letters in small or capital letters, or follow Shift

This changes only how the letters on the keys look. What a key types still follows Shift: with "Lowercase", the keys show a, b, c while Shift is on, and the letters you type are still capitals.\n\nLetters that have no capitals, and the keys of phonetic layouts such as Avro, where a and A type different letters, keep following Shift.
Follow Shift
Lowercase
Capitals
Key hint corner
Which corner of the key the long-press hint sits in
Top left
Top middle
Top right
Bottom left
Bottom middle
Bottom right
Key hint position
Distance of the corner hint from the top edge of the key
At 0 dp the hint touches the top edge of the key, and below 0 it moves up past the key\'s inner margin. Larger values move the hint down, nearer to the label. The default is 1 dp.
Key hint side position
How far in from the side of the key the hint sits. Below 0 moves it out to the edge
Key label across
Moves the letter on each key to the side, away from a large hint
Key label up or down
Moves the letter on each key down, or up below 0, away from a large hint

This changes the size of the small hint that the keyboard prints in the corner of a key. The keyboard shows the hint when \"Press and hold hints\" is on. Larger values make the hints easier to read. The default is ×1.00.
Toolbar
The bar above the keys
Toolbox
The tool grid behind the toolbar
Show the toolbar
The strip above the keys that holds the suggestions and the tools

The toolbar is the row above the keys. It shows the word suggestions while you type. At other times it shows your pinned tools, such as emoji, clipboard and cursor keys. Turn it off to give its height to the keys. The app asks you to confirm, because this also hides the suggestions and every tool.
Where the tools go
Share the suggestion strip, or use a row above it

With \"The strip\", the tools and the suggestions share one row. The tools rest there, the suggestions take the row while you type, and the arrow button changes between them. This costs no height. With \"A button\", the arrow button opens a row of tools above the suggestions, and the button closes it again. With \"Always\", that row of tools stays open. Both of these keep the tools in reach while you type, and both use the height of one more row. With \"On a swipe\", the tools share the strip again but only come when you ask: swipe up on the strip\'s toolbox button to bring them and down to put them away. Set Toolbox button under Beside the suggestions, further down this screen, for the strip to have that button.
The strip
A button
Always
On a swipe
The tools share the strip, and come up when you swipe up on its toolbox button
Toolbox button before the tools
Off leaves the toolbox to the button beside the suggestions. An open tool still shows it
Arrow to the tools
Off leaves opening and closing the tools to a swipe up and down on a toolbox button
Needs the toolbox button beside the suggestions, further down this screen
The tools and the suggestions share one row, and the arrow flips between them
The tools get a row of their own, opened and closed from the arrow
Suggestion strip
Keep the suggestion row above the tools row
Hide the strip until there are words
The tools row stays, and the suggestion row shows only while it has something to suggest

The opposite of the shared strip, where the tools give way to the words. Here the tools row is always there, and the suggestion row above or below it folds away while it is empty: before you start typing, in a field with no suggestions, or with a tool open. The first word to suggest, or a chip such as a one-time code or the paste chip, brings it back. The keyboard gets one row taller when it shows and one row shorter when it goes.

Turn this off to remove the suggestion row and keep only the row of tools. The keyboard gets one row shorter. Useful if you have turned suggestions off and the row sits empty. Everything else that appears in that row goes too: the paste chip for your last copy, one-time codes, snippet offers and other chips. Voice typing\'s compact bar still shows there while you dictate.
The tools keep a row of their own, always open
Beside the suggestions
Buttons beside the suggestions
Keep some tools in the top bar while the suggestions show

The buttons stay in the top bar, at its left end, its right end, or both. They stay while the words show, and they also stay when there are no words and the toolbar takes the bar. Emoji is the only button to begin with. Add any tool below and pick a side for each one. A tool that you also pinned on the toolbar shows one time only, in its place on the toolbar, while the toolbar shows.
Add a button
Drag to change the order. Press Left or Right to move a button to the other end
Left
Right
Side of %1$s: %2$s
A toolbox button among these buttons, so the toolbox is one press away while the suggestions show
Second toolbar
Second toolbar
A row of tools you pick, on screen whatever the strip shows

Adds a row of its own with the tools you choose below, apart from the ones pinned on the toolbar. Select all, cut, copy, paste, line start, line end, undo and redo to begin with. Turning the row on, or adding a tool to it, switches those tools on under Tools if they were off. The row stays while you type and while the strip shows suggestions, and it stays with the toolbar switched off. Its buttons look and hold like the toolbar\'s: the cursor moves repeat while held, and a hold you bound to a tool runs it. The keyboard gets one toolbar\'s height taller. A tool that takes the whole keyboard hides the row like the other bars.
Where it goes
Over the toolbar, or between the suggestions and the keys
Above the toolbar
Below the suggestions
Tools on the second toolbar
Add a tool, then drag to change the order
Tools in landscape
A column beside the keys while the phone is sideways

A phone on its side has width to spare and little height. Pick a side and, in landscape, the tools leave the top of the keyboard and stand in a column down that edge, next to the suggestions and the keys, always in reach. If the tools had a row of their own, its height goes back to the keys. The column follows the rest of the toolbar settings: your pinned tools in their order, their colors and labels, and how they fit. Portrait is unchanged.
Along the top
Left column
Right column
Swipe down to hide
Swipe down on the toolbar to close the keyboard

When this is on, a swipe down anywhere on the toolbar closes the keyboard. It is off by default, so the gesture does not start while you scroll or rearrange the toolbar. To move a tool you press and hold it, so that gesture does not close the keyboard.
Only the toolbar with a hardware keyboard
When a hardware keyboard is connected, show only the toolbar
Hide the keys when I type on the hardware keyboard
Keys you bring up with the toolbar\'s keyboard button go away at the next key you type

With only the toolbar showing, the keyboard button at the end of the toolbar brings the on-screen keys up, and the same button puts them away. With this on, typing on the physical keyboard puts them away too. Off, they stay until you tap the button again. Either way the keyboard remembers whether the keys were up for the next text box. On a physical keyboard, the shortcut leader and then Space does the same as the button. This setting is on by default.

When you connect a Bluetooth keyboard or a dock keyboard, the on-screen keys go away and only the toolbar stays. Emoji, clipboard and the other tools stay one press away while you type on the hardware keyboard. A keyboard button at the end of the toolbar brings the keys back whenever you want them. This setting is off by default.
Reverse the order for right-to-left languages
Mirror the whole toolbar when you type a right-to-left script

For right-to-left scripts, such as Arabic, Hebrew and Persian, the whole toolbar goes from right to left, so it follows the text: the toolbox button moves to the right edge and the pinned tools run back from it. This setting is off by default, so that switching between a left-to-right and a right-to-left language leaves the tools where your fingers expect them. The toolbox grid does not change either way.
Tool layout
How the pinned tools share the toolbar

Fixed size keeps the tools at one size on the left. Spread out shares the full width of the toolbar between them, like the word suggestions do. Scroll keeps each tool at a comfortable size when you pin more than fit, and lets you swipe through them. You select the tools on the toolbar from the keyboard: open the toolbox with the grid button, then press and hold a tool and drag it between the toolbar and the toolbox. With Scroll, change the order from the toolbox, because a drag inside a toolbar that scrolls is difficult.
Fixed size
Spread out
Scroll
The tools keep one size, packed to the left
The tools share the full width of the toolbar
Each tool keeps a comfortable size and the bar scrolls sideways
Toolbar top padding
Space above the tools and the suggestions
This adds space between the top edge of the keyboard and the toolbar. The default is 4 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount. Below 0 the toolbar gets shorter instead.
Toolbar bottom padding
Space between the toolbar and the keys
This adds space between the toolbar and the first row of keys. The default is 0 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount. Below 0 the toolbar gets shorter instead.
Hide the toolbar and the clipboard on the lock screen
Hide the top strip and block the clipboard while your device is locked

The keyboard opens over your lock screen when you answer a notification or use a search box there. This setting then hides the full top strip and blocks the clipboard panel. The strip holds the word suggestions and every pinned tool, so the clipboard tool and its paste chip also go. Copied text such as one-time codes and passwords stays off a screen that anyone can wake. This setting is off by default. When your device is unlocked, the keyboard does not change.
Tool labels
Show the name of each tool below its icon on the toolbar
The keyboard draws a small name below every pinned tool. Increase the toolbar height to give the labels space.
Keep labelled tools one width
Cut a long name short instead of widening its button
Color the pinned tools
Give the tools on the toolbar the colors they have in the toolbox
Label text size
Font size of the tool labels on the toolbar
Tool circle radius
How round the circle behind each toolbar tool is
20 draws a full circle behind every tool icon, like Gboard. Smaller values give rounded squares. 0 removes the background and leaves only the icons.
Tool background shape
Outline of the shape behind each toolbar tool
Tool button width
Width of each button on the toolbar
38 keeps the classic circle. Wider values stretch it into a pill, like Gboard, up to 96. The background only shows when the tool circle radius is above 0. Pairs well with the scrollable toolbar.
Tool button height
Height of each button on the toolbar
Capped at the toolbar height, %1$d dp. Raise Toolbar height under Layout & size for taller buttons.

38 is the default. Taller buttons are easier to hit. A button is never taller than the toolbar itself, so for buttons past about 40 dp raise Toolbar height as well, under Layout & size or with the resize tool.
Use my button size, not the theme\'s
The width and height here win over the width your theme sets

Your theme sets its own tool button width under Layout for this theme, and that width normally wins. Turn this on to use the sizes on this page instead, whichever theme is on. Turn it off to give the theme its width back.
Tool icon size
Size of the icon inside each tool button
Applies to the toolbar and the toolbox grid. The buttons keep their size, so the same number of tools still fit. 22 is the default.
Toolbox layout
How the toolbox draws its tools
Icons
Pills

Icons is a grid. It shows a round icon for each tool with the name below it. Pills gives each tool a wide row with round ends. The icon is on the left and the name is beside it. An arrow on the right marks the tools that open something, such as Themes and Clipboard. The other tools do their work immediately, such as Flashlight and Undo. Fewer tools fit on the screen, but you can read every name.
Toolbox grid size
Tools in each row of the toolbox grid
The toolbox is the grid behind the grid button on the toolbar. Fewer tools in a row makes each tool larger and easier to press. More tools in a row shows more tools without a scroll.
Pills per row
How many tool pills go side by side
The default is two. One gives every tool the full width, which is good for long names and large text. Three works only in landscape or on a tablet. On a smaller screen the names get cut.
Fill the pills with the tool color
Color the full pill and not only its icon

When this is off, each pill keeps the background of the theme and only the icon shows the color of the tool. When it is on, the pill gets that color. The icon and the name change to a color that you can read on it: white on most colors, almost black on pale colors. This needs \"Colorful tool icons\" (Settings → Tools) to be on. With that setting off, there is no color to fill the pill with.
Swipe the toolbox in pages
Fixed pages that you swipe sideways, and not one grid that scrolls

When this is off, the toolbox is one grid that scrolls up and down. When it is on, the toolbox becomes pages that you swipe between. Dots below the grid show your position. Every tool then keeps the same place, so you can find it from memory. To move a tool to another page, drag it and hold it against the side edge of the toolbox until the page turns.
Toolbox search
A search button on the toolbar while the toolbox is open
Back puts a tool\'s keys down first
The next Back closes the tool

With the keys up under a tool\'s own box, such as Translate or find and replace, the first Back takes the keys down so the whole tool shows, and the second closes the tool. Off, Back closes the tool at once. Either way, the keyboard button at the end of the box\'s suggestion strip puts the keys down.

While the toolbox is open, the toolbar shows a search button. Tapping it opens the search over the whole keyboard, with a back button that returns to the toolbox. Type a tool\'s name to find it, wherever it is, folders included. Turn this off to leave the toolbox without a search.
Search button at the far end
Put the toolbox search at the far end of the toolbar, away from the back button

When this is on, the search button sits at the far end of the toolbar, after your pinned tools, so a tap meant for the back button does not open the search. When it is off, the search button sits right next to the back button.
Toolbox order
Put the tools in your own order, or the ones you use first
Your order
Most used
Recently used
A to Z
Space around each tool
Above and below each tool in the toolbox grid. Less fits more rows on a page

Your order is the order you make by dragging tools around the toolbox. Most used puts the tools you open most often first. Recently used puts the tool you opened last first. Tools you have never opened come after them, in your order. The toolbox sorts itself each time it opens, so tools do not move while you tap them. A folder sits where its first tool falls, and keeps its own order inside. Dragging a tool still changes your order, and you get it back when you choose Your order again.
Search order before typing
How the toolbox search lists the tools until you type

The toolbox search lists every tool until you type something. Your order lists them the way you arranged the toolbox. Most used puts the tools you open most often first. Recently used puts the tool you opened last first. Once you type, the names that start with what you typed come first.
Tools per page
How many tools each toolbox page holds
Select a multiple of your row size to fill the last row of every page. If you select more tools than the panel can show, the page scrolls as well as swipes.
%1$d per row
%1$d per page
Turn off the toolbar?

The full top strip goes away. You lose the word suggestions and fast access to every pinned tool, such as emoji, clipboard and cursor keys. The keys use the free height. You can turn the toolbar on again here at any time.
Suggestion text size
How large the words in the suggestion strip are

Key labels have their own size setting and the suggestions above them did not, so large keys could still come with small suggestions. This also sizes the candidate row for Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese input, since it is the same row in a different mode. This setting is 100% by default.
Suggestion spacing
The gap on each side of a word in the suggestion strip

Lower it to fit more of a long word before it has to shrink, or to pack more suggestions onto a narrow screen. Raise it to keep neighbouring words from reading as one when the strip scrolls. This setting is 6 dp by default.
Autocorrect word color
Color of the word that autocorrect will put in for a space

The strip draws its first suggestion in bold. Pick a color here and that word takes the color only when autocorrect has decided to put it in for you when you type a space. A bold word without the color is the top suggestion, and a space keeps what you typed. The other suggestions keep the theme color. Reset the row to follow the theme again.
New word color
Color of a word that no word list or your dictionary knows yet

Pick a color here and a word on the strip that is in no word list, not in your personal dictionary, not one of your contacts and not accepted by the spell checker takes it. That is usually the word you are typing, so you can see that it would be new to the dictionary before you add it from its hold menu or the keyboard learns it on its own. The color goes as soon as the word is learned or added. The autocorrect word color wins where both apply. Not used on a layout that turns your keys into another script. Reset the row to follow the theme again.
Toolbox label size
The name under each tool in the full tool panel
By default these follow the toolbar label size, so the two agree. Set a size here to make the toolbox names larger or smaller on their own. This setting follows the toolbar by default.
Follow toolbar
Reset appearance
Put every setting on this screen back to its default

The key corner radius, the label and hint sizes and the hint position go back to their defaults. Your theme, your font and your icon pack are not affected: they have their own screens. The toolbar and the toolbox have resets of their own.
Reset toolbar
Put every setting on this screen back to its default
The toolbar, its labels, the suggestion strip and the tool shape go back to their defaults. Which tools are pinned is not affected.
Reset toolbox
Put every setting on this screen back to its default
The grid layout, the columns, the paging and the label size go back to their defaults. The order of the tools, and which tools are switched on, are not affected.
Set by your theme \"%1$s\". Change it there, under Layout for this theme.
Reset toolbox order
Put the tools in the toolbox grid back in their original order
The tools in the toolbox grid go back to the order they shipped in. Which tools are switched on, and which are pinned to the toolbar, are not affected.
Rearrange by dragging
Press and hold a tool on the toolbar, then drag it to a new place
Press and hold delay
How long you hold a tool before the hold counts

This sets how long you press a tool on the toolbar or in the toolbox before the press counts as a hold. A hold runs the action you chose under Press and hold on the toolbar on the tool\'s own settings page, opens that settings page, or picks the tool up to move it. At System, the keyboard uses the touch and hold delay from your phone\'s accessibility settings.
System

When this is on, a press and hold that moves picks the tool up so you can drop it elsewhere on the toolbar. When it is off, a press and hold that moves stays a press and hold, and the toolbox is where you rearrange the toolbar. Turn it off if a hold keeps turning into a drag by accident.
